overview: The Republic of the Congo is a country in Central Africa, sometimes called Congo-Brazzaville to tell it apart from its larger neighbour, DR Congo. Its capital and largest city is Brazzaville, which faces Kinshasa across the Congo river. It became independent from France in 1960, and oil is its main export.

geography.text: Rainforest covers much of the country, especially the north, which is part of the Congo Basin. The Congo and Ubangi rivers form much of the eastern border. The south has plateaus and savanna, and a short Atlantic coast around the port of Pointe-Noire.

history.text: The Kingdom of Loango and the Tio kingdom traded along the coast and rivers. France colonised the region in the 1880s, and Brazzaville became the capital of French Equatorial Africa and, in the Second World War, of Free France. The Republic of the Congo became independent in 1960.

events.title: Treaty with France
events.text: Pierre Savorgnan de Brazza signs a treaty with the Tio king.

events.title: Capital of Free France
events.text: De Gaulle makes Brazzaville a base of Free France.

events.title: Independence
events.text: The Republic of the Congo becomes independent.

government.text: The Republic of the Congo is a presidential republic. Denis Sassou Nguesso has been President for most of the time since 1979.

economy.text: Oil makes up most of the country's exports. Timber is also important, and the economy has struggled with debt.

culture.text: Brazzaville and Kinshasa face each other across the Congo River, the closest pair of capital cities in the world apart from Rome and Vatican City. The Congo shares a love of rumba music and sapeur fashion with its larger neighbour.

items.title: Twin capitals
items.text: Brazzaville and Kinshasa sit on opposite banks of the river.

items.title: Odzala-Kokoua
items.text: A national park home to western lowland gorillas.

sport.text: Football is the most popular sport, and the Congo won the Africa Cup of Nations in 1972.
